regulation: Real Decreto 1055/2022 de envases y residuos de envases
title: Spain: authorised representative for non-established producers
summary: A producer not established in Spain must appoint a representante autorizado to carry the packaging obligations. Where none is appointed, responsibility passes to the first distributor in Spain — which is why a seller may believe they are covered when they are not.

required_evidence.label: Signed appointment of the representante autorizado

sources.title: Real Decreto 1055/2022, de 27 de diciembre, de envases y residuos de envases (BOE-A-2022-22690)
sources.note: Fetched the statute directly. Art. 17.2, verbatim: 'Los productores de productos que estén establecidos en otro Estado miembro o en terceros países y que comercialicen productos en España, deberán designar a una persona física o jurídica en territorio español como representante autorizado...' and its third paragraph: 'En el caso de que los productores de producto no hayan designado un representante autorizado en España, el primer distribuidor o comerciante del producto envasado con sede en España será, subsidiariamente, el sujeto responsable...' -- both the mandatory-appointment duty and the first-distributor fallback this row's summary already describes are confirmed word for word, resolving the 13 Sept draft's only open question. NOT modelled, found in the same article's paragraph 5: for transport packaging used in distance sales, the courier/parcel company (or the e-commerce platform, where it facilitates a third party's sale) fulfils the producer's financial/information obligations on the producer's behalf -- but this is scoped narrowly to shipping/transport packaging only, not the AR duty as a whole, so left out of applies_when.
